messages:
Anya: Heads-up — Customer X just asked for a staged rollout plan that guarantees no PII leaves EU during their initial 2-week canary. They want feature-flagged opt-in per-tenant + automated rollback hooks. Need product + infra decision: do we scope as 'Private-only' or support hosted per-region canary?
Sam: @Anya do we know which model variant they want? small quantized or our full FP16? that affects latency/infra.
Anya: They prefer our standard hosted LLMv2 (FP16) for quality. They're okay with temporarily routing EU traffic to EU-hosted instances only for canary. Key ask = telemetry gate + manual kill-switch. Deadline = customer pilot in 3 weeks.
Lina: Telemetry gates: propose these minimum signals before moving from 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% slices: p95 latency, 5xx/error-rate, token-cost delta, and a small prompt-quality regression set (10 prompts, human-reviewed). If any breach, auto-hold and notify.
Michael: +1. Operational plan suggestion: 1) enable flag for 1% EU tenants on EU-region nodes; 2) 48h canary window with metric gates; 3) 7-day progressive ramp to 100% with daily review. Fallback: route to fallback-model-small or to dedicated default endpoint.
Priya: Customer cares about SLA during pilot. They want a fallback path that won’t degrade UX badly. Can we quantify fallback latency delta?
Michael: We should commit to max p95 delta of +120ms vs baseline or automatic failover to cached responses (prefix caching) for bursty flows. Fallback-model-small has ~2x latency for some long prompts — must warn customer.
Sam: Scope negotiation: supporting EU-hosted canaries for hosted customers adds infra ops (region provisioning + secrets). Alternative: recommend Redwood Dedicated for this customer as contractual option. Which path do we prefer?
Anya: Let's keep hosted option in scope if we can reuse existing EU capacity and add a 'regional-only canary' flag. If infra cost estimate > X, we push Dedicated option. Priya: customer likely okay with committed cost for pilot.
Lina: Flag shape proposal (example):
```
{ "flag": "tenant_regional_canary", "targeting": {"region": "eu-west-1", "tenants": ["cust-x"]}, "slices": [1,10,50,100], "rollback": {"auto_hold_on": ["p95_latency>300","error_rate>0.2%"], "manual_kill": true} }
```
Michael: Add metric ownership + alerting: infra owns latency gates, product owns quality regressions, CSE/Customer success owns go/no-go. We must document escalation path in runbook.
Priya: I'll draft customer-facing runbook bullet points and ask legal about data residency language. Timeline: draft by EOD Friday?
Anya: EOD Friday works. Also need an SLO for canary: no sustained >1.5x error rate increase for 2 consecutive 5-min windows. Add to checklist.
Sam: For prioritization: is this a high-touch enterprise sale? If yes, we can move a small infra sprint ahead of backlog. We should ask sales to confirm.
Priya: Sales confirmed high-touch pilot and will sign a 3-month pilot MSA. They expect rollout support from eng for first week.
release-bot: deploy-schedule: scheduled eu-canary-blue at 2026-04-02T09:00Z, canary window 48h; approvers required: Anya, Michael, Lina.
Anya: Next actions: Lina + Michael to write runbook + flag schema; Priya to get legal and sales signoff; Sam to triage infra estimate. We'll reconvene Thu 11am to freeze scope. :thumbsup:
